Your profile is strongly technical (AI/ML projects, Python, Sentinel data) while the role focuses on R&D management and strategic road-mapping in a business/policy category.
why_apply: Gain insight into ESA technology strategy processes even if not selected
Network with Luxembourgish delegates and ESA staff in Darmstadt
required_skills: Luxembourgish nationality
Recent Master's or equivalent in engineering/management
Experience in technology road-mapping or R&D programme management
gaps: Nationality requirement not met
Still early-stage BSc student, not graduate level
No demonstrated experience in strategic road-mapping or programme management
Profile is technical AI/data rather than business/policy

checklist.task: Verify Luxembourgish nationality eligibility on the ESA jobs portal for this specific vacancy
checklist.done_when: Eligibility confirmed or ruled out in writing from ESA

opportunities.title: CubeSats: Fly Your Satellite!
opportunities.summary: Next cycle expected to open in 2027 Contact: cubesats@esa.int.
opportunities.deadline_text: Next cycle expected to open in 2027

evaluation.justification: Your AI/Data Science background and satellite-data projects (Sentinel-1 flood mapping, hfarm-satellite-tracking, ESA-Scout repo) show genuine interest and relevant technical skills, but the CubeSats programme targets students with core aerospace or space-systems engineering experience that you currently lack. At this early stage of your BSc you would be a stretch applicant even when the next cycle opens in 2027.
why_apply: Hands-on CubeSat development experience directly aligned with your existing satellite-data and hardware projects
Access to ESA facilities, testing and launch opportunities unavailable at university level
Networking with European space-engineering teams and potential future employers
required_skills: Spacecraft systems engineering and AIV (assembly, integration, verification)
CubeSat platform subsystems (ADCS, EPS, OBC, communications)
Team-based project management under ESA standards and reviews
Hardware prototyping and environmental testing
gaps: No formal aerospace, mechanical or electrical engineering coursework
Limited documented experience with satellite hardware or flight software
Early-stage BSc student (still <2 years completed) versus typical successful applicants
No prior participation in ESA Academy or equivalent space-hands-on programmes

checklist.task: Complete at least one university module or online course in spacecraft subsystems or orbital mechanics
checklist.done_when: Transcript or certificate obtained

checklist.task: Extend the ESA-Scout or hfarm-satellite-tracking repository with documented CubeSat-relevant code (e.g., attitude determination or onboard data handling)
checklist.done_when: Public GitHub commit history with README and tests

checklist.task: Join or form a university CubeSat / rocketry team and contribute to a hardware deliverable
checklist.done_when: Team membership confirmed and subsystem report produced

checklist.task: Prepare a 2-page project proposal outlining a CubeSat payload that leverages your AI/ML pipeline experience
checklist.done_when: PDF ready for future application

opportunities.title: Rocket and Balloon Experiments: REXUS/BEXUS
opportunities.summary: Next call for proposals expected to open in June 2027 Contact: rexus-bexus@esa.int.
opportunities.deadline_text: Next call for proposals expected to open in June 2027

evaluation.justification: Your AI/data science background and satellite-related projects (floodfusion, hfarm-satellite-tracking) show relevant technical skills and ESA interest, but REXUS/BEXUS primarily seeks teams proposing physical experiments in space systems, rocketry or atmospheric science. At this stage in your BSc you lack demonstrated hardware integration or experiment-proposal experience for sounding rockets/balloons, making this a stretch application.
why_apply: Direct exposure to ESA sounding-rocket and balloon flight opportunities
Chance to integrate your AI/ML pipeline work into a real space payload
Networking with European student teams and ESA engineers
required_skills: Experiment proposal and systems engineering for rockets/balloons
Hardware integration and testing (sensors, power, recovery)
Team leadership across technical disciplines
Knowledge of space environment constraints
gaps: No prior rocket or balloon payload development experience
Early in BSc (second year at call opening) with limited space-systems coursework
Portfolio focused on software/AI rather than physical experiment hardware

checklist.task: Study the last three REXUS/BEXUS experiment reports that used onboard data processing or imaging
checklist.done_when: One-page summary of technical requirements and lessons learned written

checklist.task: Draft a one-page concept note linking your Synapse or floodfusion pipeline to a balloon-borne atmospheric measurement
checklist.done_when: Concept note reviewed by a mentor or professor

checklist.task: Contact rexus-bexus@esa.int with a short email expressing interest and requesting past student team contacts
checklist.done_when: Reply received and logged

checklist.task: Join or form a multidisciplinary team including at least one aerospace/mechanical engineering student before June 2027
checklist.done_when: Team roster and roles documented

opportunities.title: Hardware testing: Test Opportunities

evaluation.justification: Your AI/Data Science background and satellite-data projects (Sentinel-1 fusion, hfarm-satellite-tracking) show genuine interest in ESA topics, but the role centers on hands-on hardware testing for space systems rather than software or data pipelines. At this early stage of your BSc you lack documented experience with electronics qualification, environmental testing, or CubeSat hardware standards that the programme expects. The ESA-Scout repository name and plasma-toroid build are positive signals, yet they do not yet close the gap for a competitive application.
why_apply: Direct exposure to ESA CubeSat testing facilities and engineers
Opportunity to add space-hardware qualification experience to an AI-focused CV
Networking with the cubesats@esa.int team for future ESA Academy calls
required_skills: Hardware testing and qualification procedures
Electronics or mechanical integration for small satellites
CubeSat or nanosatellite standards knowledge
Hands-on environmental or functional testing
gaps: No formal hardware-testing or space-qualification experience listed
Degree programme is AI & Data Science, not aerospace or electronics engineering
Limited evidence of working with flight hardware or test campaigns
Early in BSc (expected graduation 2028) so few advanced engineering credits

checklist.task: Email cubesats@esa.int with a one-page summary of your Sentinel-1 fusion work and plasma-toroid build, asking for next Test Opportunities cycle details
checklist.done_when: Email sent and any reply logged

checklist.task: Complete the ESA Academy MOOC 'CubeSats – From Design to Launch' and note test-related modules
checklist.done_when: Certificate obtained and key test procedures summarised

checklist.task: Document the Xenon Plasma Toroid project with test measurements, safety notes and photos for a future application portfolio
checklist.done_when: Two-page technical note uploaded to GitHub

key_deadlines.label: Contact cubesats@esa.int for updated Test Opportunities timeline
